content: With 6–9 HCP and 3+ cards in partner's suit, make a simple raise (2 of partner's suit). It shows a fit and a minimum responding hand.
With 10–12 HCP and 4+ card support, make a limit raise (3 of partner's suit). It invites game and shows a strong fit.
With 6–10 HCP, no fit for partner, and no new suit you can bid at the 1-level, respond 1NT. It keeps the auction low and shows values.
With 6+ HCP and a 4+ card suit that ranks higher than partner's, bid that new suit at the 1-level. New suits are forcing and explore for the best fit.
With fewer than 6 HCP, pass partner's opening. You lack the strength to respond safely.
Myth: “I should always bid a new suit, even with support.” When you have a good fit and a minimum, showing the fit with a raise is usually clearer than inventing a new suit.
Partner opens 1♠. You hold ♠Q93 ♥K74 ♦J852 ♣T63 (7 HCP, 3 spades). Raise to 2♠.
Partner opens 1♠. You hold ♠52 ♥K843 ♦Q762 ♣J43 (6 HCP, no fit). Respond 1NT.
How many cards do you hold in partner's suit? Do you have a fit?
Count your points. Are you minimum (6–9), invitational (10–12), or too weak to bid?
